strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout in src/cart.js (cartTotal, bulkDiscount): 10% bulk discount at 10+ items in total, the SAVE5 coupon after the bulk discount with goods floored at $0, other coupons refused, and $4.99 shipping unless discounted goods reach $50 (empty cart costs $0). Unit tests with vitest must prove each rule and its boundaries. Reading the code shows two likely defects: bulkDiscount uses `> BULK_THRESHOLD` (exactly 10 items gets no discount), and the coupon check uses `in`, so inherited names such as `toString` are accepted rather than refused.
inScope: cartTotal and bulkDiscount in src/cart.js: bulk discount, coupon, shipping rules and their boundaries
outOfScope: UI/checkout pages (none exist in this repo)
subtotal line arithmetic, already covered by test/cart.test.js
assumptions: Refusing a coupon means cartTotal throws; the test identifies the refusal by the code it submitted appearing in the error message, since there is no error code.
Coupon codes are case-sensitive as written in the ticket (SAVE5); a cart with items whose goods are reduced to $0 still pays $4.99 shipping, per AC3's 'otherwise'.
Failing assertions that match the ticket but not the code are kept and marked it.fails, with record_defect.
openQuestions: Should coupon codes be case-insensitive (e.g. 'save5')? The code treats them as case-sensitive; not tested.
Should a coupon of an empty string or null be refused or treated as no coupon? Not tested.

risks.description: Off-by-one at the 10-item threshold: the code uses > instead of >=
risks.mitigation: TC1 checks exactly 10 items across several lines

risks.description: Coupon lookup via `in` accepts Object prototype names (toString), producing NaN totals
risks.mitigation: TC7 checks such a code is refused

risks.description: Order of bulk discount vs coupon, and shipping threshold measured before discounts
risks.mitigation: TC4 uses figures where the order changes the total; TC10 checks the threshold is on discounted goods

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 gets none.
SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount, goods never below $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when goods after discounts are $50 or more, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs $0.

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: carts of 10 or more items get 10% off. In src/cart.js, bulkDiscount checks `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items is charged full price.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:10,quantity:4},{price:10,quantity:6}]) returns 100. The expected total is 90. The test is marked it.fails and passes as an expected failure.

defects.title: Coupon codes named after Object prototype properties are accepted (total NaN)
defects.description: AC2: any coupon other than SAVE5 must be refused with an error. In src/cart.js, cartTotal checks `coupon in COUPONS`, which is also true for inherited names such as 'toString'. The code then subtracts a function, and the total comes out NaN.
defects.evidence: cartTotal([{price:20,quantity:1}], {coupon:'toString'}) does not throw. It returns NaN. The test is marked it.fails and passes as an expected failure.
